html:
The Siege of Kyiv ended on 6 December 1240, when a Mongol army under Batu Khan stormed the city, then one of the largest in Europe, and destroyed most of it.

The Mongols had already taken the northeastern cities of Rus, such as Ryazan and Vladimir. At Kyiv they broke the walls with siege engines, and the last defenders died in the Church of the Tithes, which collapsed under the crowd. A papal envoy who passed six years later reported only a couple of hundred houses left. Rus lands came under the Golden Horde. Kyiv lost its leading role, and the centre of power moved to Galicia-Volhynia in the west, to Lithuania, and to Moscow in the north. The siege ended the age of Yaroslav and his heirs.
sum: The Siege of Kyiv ended on 6 December 1240, when a Mongol army under Batu Khan stormed the city, then one of the largest in Europe, and destroyed most of it.
